label: Plant-set cheese
comment: Set by an enzyme from a plant: a third way, after rennet and acid.

about.text: Cheese set not by rennet from a calf's stomach or by acid but by an enzyme from a plant: cardoon thistle flowers in the cheeses of Portugal and Spain, Calotropis in West Africa's wagashi, papaya latex in Indonesia's dangke, ginger juice in southern China's ginger milk curd.

A few cheeses of Portugal, Spain and West Africa set with thistle or other plants. My own rough estimate.

facts.v: Flower pistils, soaked and used as the coagulant; aspartic proteinases: cardosins A–H plus cyprosin

Sheep or goat milk set at about 30 °C with cardoon or thistle; curd not cooked, pressed and ripened for weeks to months (Azeitão about 20 d, Serra da Estrela at least 30 d, Torta del Casar at least 60 d)
Milk heated to 59 °C for 20 min; coagulum then cooked at about 91 °C for 34 min
Sliced papaya leaves, stems or unripe fruit boiled with the milk
Benin (wagashi, gassirè), Nigeria (wara, warankasi), Ghana, Burkina Faso, Niger, Togo
Almost all plant milk coagulants are aspartic proteases; cysteine and serine proteases can also clot milk
Cardosin A attacks κ-casein and gives softer textures; cardosin B is less specific and linked to firmness defects
Strong proteolysis gives lower yields, bitterness and texture defects, so plant coagulants are used on a small or semi-industrial scale
Torta del Casar, Torta de la Serena (Spain); Nisa (Portugal)
27–32 % of the milk; moulded in colanders
Brined overnight, wrapped in banana leaves that mask the papaya bitterness; no temperature given
